stem:
Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence.

The workers ___ lunch at noon.
hints: Look at the subject. Is it one worker or more than one?
Find the subject: "workers". The -s at the end means more than one.
With one person or thing, an action verb takes -s. With two or more, it does not. Words ending in -en or -ing need a helper word, so they cannot be the verb alone. Choose the form that fits.

solution.methodName: Count the subject, then match the verb

steps.action: Find the subject: "workers". It ends in -s, so it means more than one.
steps.why: For most nouns, an -s at the end means plural (more than one).

steps.action: A plural subject takes the verb with no -s: the workers eat.
steps.why: For verbs it works the other way. The verb takes -s only when the subject is one person or thing, as in "The worker eats."

steps.action: "eaten" and "eating" cannot be the verb alone.
steps.why: They need a helper, as in "have eaten" or "are eating".

steps.action: The answer is "eat": The workers eat lunch at noon.

trapNotes.eats: Eats goes with one person: the worker eats. Workers means more than one, so drop the -s from the verb.
trapNotes.eaten: Eaten needs a helper, as in "have eaten." It cannot be the verb by itself.
trapNotes.eating: Eating needs a helper, as in "are eating." It cannot be the verb by itself.
